hero.kicker: AI-directed work / CS + physics at CSULB
hero.title: I direct AI agents to carry out what I ask.
hero.lede: AI agents carry out whatever I direct, software included. That work has included running a home estate of several machines, producing research reports, disk and ops cleanup, and building this site. I set the bar and decide what ships. Every demo below runs, and its source is public so you can check the work.

demos.name: TowerOps Airspace Lab
demos.line: A traffic-management simulation where you create flights, change their paths and see where conflicts develop. Synthetic demo, not operational ATC.
demos.detail: A planner proposes adjustments; each simulated change goes through approval and readback, with an audit trail. The actual AdvisoryPlanner and ControlRoom run in-browser via CPython/WebAssembly, not a mock or replay. It uses synthetic or visitor-provided data and is not operational air-traffic-control software.

desktop.alt: TowerOps simplified desktop view: two crossing flights and a three-step planner, approval and readback flow. Advanced controls are collapsed.

mobile.alt: TowerOps simplified mobile view: two crossing flights and a three-step planner, approval and readback flow. Advanced controls are collapsed.

demos.name: RecallWeave
demos.line: An offline learning toolkit: adaptive lessons, course downloads, authoring tools and interactive science, mathematics and computing labs.
demos.detail: The learner exposes Bayesian model estimates, not grades or demonstrated learning gains. Work with local lesson files and explicit downloads; no account or cloud service. Submitted to ForgeHacks 2026 (Devpost entry 1221781).

desktop.alt: RecallWeave on desktop: a question about cellular energy with four answer choices, a concept map, and live mastery bars.

mobile.alt: RecallWeave on a phone after six questions: the learning trace with per-concept mastery estimates.

engine.title: Hamon Engine
engine.tagline: A Rust game engine built for AI agents
engine.line: Most engines assume a person at the editor, so agents guess from screenshots. Hamon exposes exact state over MCP and is deterministic: agents can rerun and compare changes. Agents also drive the next feature when the engine falls short.

slot.title: Lanternwake
slot.line: The latest playable Hamon Engine build. The engine repository remains private and is not linked here; only the compiled browser runtime is published.

games.name: Lanternwake
games.line: Restore three lanterns on a small 3D island, then return to the stone arch at dawn. Keyboard and touch controls; WebGPU required, no account or install.

build.evidence: Played to victory and restarted with real keyboard input (desktop) and touch buttons (phone-size viewport) in Chromium, zero console errors. Physical phone and Safari untested.

games.name: Spire of Octaves
games.line: My own world, told through stories, music, games and animation. A vertical world born from an unfinished sacred song, where matter remembers intent and new floors are still being composed beneath the people who live there. Its first story, *Seamwork*, is a short story published on Royal Road.

how.title: How it gets built
how.line: AI agents carry out whatever I direct, software included. I set the bar and decide what ships.

steps.name: I pick the work
steps.line: A research report, an ops problem, or software that needs building. Whatever needs doing.

steps.name: I set the bar
steps.line: A short brief: what it must do, what it must not do, and how we will know it works.

steps.name: Agents carry it out
steps.line: AI agents carry out the task I direct, whether it is software, research reports, or operations work.

steps.name: Checks before claims
steps.line: I check the result against the bar. Tests and CI matter for software; other work needs its own evidence.

steps.name: I decide what ships
steps.line: Software links to source where it is public. Reports and ops work ship when I decide they clear the bar.

projects.name: CaptureSuite
projects.line: Windows-first multimodal research capture: a daemon, versioned worker plugins and sealed session packages, with an offline QC demo on synthetic EMG/IMU data.

projects.name: CanvasPilot
projects.line: An MCP server and CLI for Canvas LMS that rides the browser session you already have, for schools that disable personal access tokens.

projects.name: workflow-checks
projects.line: Three small Python checks for back-office paperwork (utility bills, freight detention, PT authorizations), run on synthetic data with file:row evidence.

projects.name: Multi-agent Fan-out Engine
projects.line: A public-safe reference core for dependency plans, SQLite dispatch custody and reconcile-not-replay. Local adapter tests, not claims about production capacity.

lines: I study computer science and physics at Cal State Long Beach, with a minor in biology. I'm a BUILD Scholar working toward MD/PhD training.
I direct AI agents across more than software: running a home estate of several machines, producing research reports, disk and ops cleanup, and building this site. I set the bar and decide what ships.

My research experience spans gait and rehabilitation, behavioral neurobiology, protein molecular dynamics, and collaborative surgical-ergonomics work. I'm interested in measurement, reproducible analysis and scientific software.

Checks come before claims. I keep runnable examples, source and explicit limits with the work. Research contributions are collaborative; synthetic demos are not evidence of clinical validity, learning gains or savings on someone else's data.

contact.line: The fastest way to reach me or see what I'm working on is GitHub.
